name: LogRocket
summary: LogRocket is a session replay and error monitoring service that records what a person did in your app so you can watch what led to a bug.

free_plan_covers.note: There's no permanent free plan anymore, only a 14-day free trial with full features and no credit card required.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The Core plan starts at $69/month for 10,000 sessions a month billed monthly, with unlimited analytics, error and log events.

portability.note: The recording SDK is proprietary with no OpenTelemetry support, but LogRocket has a documented export API and an automatic hourly export of session and event data to your own Snowflake, BigQuery or S3 warehouse as open Parquet files.

uptime_checks.note: LogRocket doesn't check whether your site is reachable from outside; it only records sessions and errors from people who actually load your app.

session_replay.note: Session replay is LogRocket's core feature, recording a video-like playback of what a person did; fields can be marked data-private and password fields are never recorded.

setup.step: Sign up for LogRocket (14-day free trial, no credit card) and create a project to get its app ID.
Install the SDK with npm install --save logrocket.
Call LogRocket.init() with your app ID once, from a client-only entry point (for example a small component that only runs on mount), never from server code.
Mark any input or element that shows personal data with the data-private attribute so LogRocket never records it.

builder_notes: The docs pass the app ID straight to LogRocket.init(); store it in a browser-readable environment variable (with your framework's public prefix) instead of hardcoding it, even though it isn't a secret.
Only call LogRocket.init() in client-side code that runs once; calling it during server rendering or more than once breaks session capture.
Turn on the private-by-default option, or add data-private and use requestSanitizer/responseSanitizer, before recording any page or network call with personal data.
